title: Terraform module for Private control plane (EKS) provisioning and upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module to provision Redwood Private control planes on AWS EKS within customer VPCs. The module must: (1) create/control EKS cluster and nodegroups with option for nodegroup autoscaling or Karpenter, (2) wire up IAM roles and OIDC provider, (3) create supporting networking (private subnets, NAT, route tables) or consume existing VPC/subnets, (4) integrate KMS for EBS/Secrets encryption and optional HSM/KMS key aliases, (5) expose a private API endpoint and optional bastion/jumpbox provisioning, (6) install required add-ons via Helm (aws-node, coredns, kube-proxy, vpc-cni, kube-prometheus-stack), (7) emit health metrics and health-check endpoints for control plane components, and (8) provide upgrade/rollout primitives (canary kubelet upgrades, drain/cordon policies, post-upgrade smoke checks). The module must be opinionated enough for production deployments but configurable for enterprise needs (private endpoint only, dedicated subnets, custom AMIs, FIPS/KMS settings). Deliverable: Terraform v1.5-compatible module with examples, integration tests, docs, and an upgrade playbook for major/minor EKS kernel/patch operations.
acceptance_criteria: Module deploys a private EKS control plane into an existing VPC using a single terraform apply with example vars
Cluster has private API endpoint and optionally disabled public endpoint (configurable)
IAM roles and OIDC provider created with least-privilege policies and documented overrides
EBS volumes and Kubernetes secrets encrypted with customer KMS key when provided
Module exposes outputs for kubeconfig, cluster endpoint, nodegroup ASG IDs, and CloudWatch log group ARNs
Automated post-provision health checks run (nodes Ready, kube-system pods Running, control plane API responsive), failing apply if smoke checks fail when strict mode enabled
Upgrade workflow implemented as documented Terraform pattern and example: canary nodegroup, drain/cordon hooks, and rollback instructions
Integration tests pass in CICD (plan/apply/destroy in a test account) and there is a sample usage repo
Security review completed and SSM/KMS/HSM integration verified by Security team
tasks: Draft module interface (variables/outputs) and naming conventions
Implement core EKS resource creation using aws_eks_cluster and managed node groups or eksctl/karpenter toggle
Implement optional VPC creation or VPC data-source consumption path
Add IAM role and OIDC provider resources, generate least-privilege policies
Integrate KMS key acceptance and kms_key_id validation; support import of existing key
Add helm_release resources to install required addons and setup Prometheus metrics
Add cloudwatch metrics and create default CloudWatch dashboards for control plane health
Implement post-apply smoke checks (terraform local-exec or external test harness)
Document upgrade procedure and implement terraform patterns for canary upgrades
Add unit/integration tests and CI pipeline job; run test in sandbox account
Prepare runbook and rollback playbook for on-call and SRE
decisions: Use managed node groups as default, expose option to enable Karpenter for burst workloads
Default to private API endpoint enabled; public endpoint disabled by default for Private customers
Use Terraform modules + Terratest for integration tests rather than in-module provisioners for smoke checks
Expose strict_mode boolean that makes smoke checks fail the apply when set to true
KMS integration will accept both AWS-managed and customer-managed (CMK) keys; HSM support documented but gated behind manual steps

risk: Medium. Improper IAM or KMS configuration can lead to data exposure or inability to rotate keys. Upgrades carry risk of node eviction and service disruption if drain policies are misconfigured.
notes: Follow existing internal module patterns for inputs/outputs and tag resources with customer and env tags. Coordinate with SRE for CI sandbox quotas (we need 3 t3.large nodes for tests by 2026-03-20). Include terraform-docs generated markdown for every release.
runbook_summary: Runbook includes pre-checks (VPC CIDR, subnet mapping), backup steps for cluster autoscaler config, a canary upgrade procedure (create canary nodegroup, migrate 10% of pods, validate, then rollout), and rollback steps to restore previous node template
